1. The pitch

Command, don't configure. c003

One line: Rebind is a free, programmable input layer for Windows and macOS. You script your keyboard and mouse in Luau, and you can add Rebind Link when you need real USB hardware output. c002, c012, c005

Positioning: a device-macro, automation, and accessibility multitool for your PC or Mac: one place to remap keys, record macros, automate input, and run accessibility recipes on the keyboard and mouse you already own. c030, c069, c085, c116 Supported today on Windows 10/11 64-bit and macOS 13+ on Apple Silicon. c013, c015

Short description: Vendor software lets you select behavior. Rebind lets you write it. c008 Rebind runs Luau scripts that decide what your keys, clicks, and scroll do: remap a key, bind a shortcut to a mouse button, record and replay a macro, expand text, or give each app its own layout. c004, c067, c069, c072, c076 The app is free, and local scripts need no account and no hardware. c012, c024 When a script needs more, such as changing mouse movement, using a game controller, or sending output as a real USB device, Rebind Link or BYOH adds a hardware mode. c031, c032, c029 It works with the standard-HID keyboard and mouse you already own, any brand. c116

2. What it is, in plain words

VISUAL V2 · FOR CREATIVE STUDIO
One simple diagram: input, then your Luau script, then output, shown twice. Software mode: OS hooks in, SendInput (Windows) or CGEvent (macOS) out. Hardware mode: devices into Rebind Link or BYOH, real USB HID out. STILL NEEDED: not in Creative Studio's v1 set. Existing vectors to build from: E:\Marketing Repo\Rebind\brand-vectors\keyboard.svg, mouse.svg, rebind-link.svg, usb-cable.svg.

Frame 02, "A script you can read." Caption on the frame: Simulated UI / animated mock-up.

Luau scripting

  • Scripts are written in Luau, and they rewrite keys and clicks. c004
  • The first documented script is one line: rb.bind.remap("CapsLock", "Escape"). c061 A remap can also send a chord, like Kp1 to LCtrl+LAlt+1. c062
  • Handlers react to keys, buttons, and scroll (rb.on), and Luau coroutines (rb.run, rb.sleep, rb.async) handle timed sequences. c067, c070
  • A script can target one app with a process= or window= modeline or a when callback, and use focus and blur handlers to act differently per app. c072, c073
  • Built in: networking (rb.net), overlays (rb.overlay), UI panels (rb.ui), and screen, window, and macro APIs. c074, c077, c078
  • Scripts are plain .lua / .luau files you can edit in VS Code, sort into subfolders, and track with git. c087, c088
  • The same scripts move between Windows and macOS, but not every API is identical on both. c017

Software mode (free, the default)

  • Free, no hardware, and no account for local scripts. c024
  • Rebind reads input through operating-system hooks and sends output through SendInput on Windows or CGEvent on macOS. c026, c028 It sees input before your apps do. c038
  • It can remap and block keys, buttons, and scroll, and record macros. c030, c113
  • It handles mouse buttons, not mouse movement. c068
  • It works with a laptop's built-in keyboard and trackpad. c107

Hardware mode (Rebind Link or BYOH)

  • Hardware mode uses Rebind Link or BYOH with a signed-in account and device activation. c025
  • Your attached keyboard, mouse, and controllers are forwarded into an isolated capture VM before events reach scripts, and output leaves as real USB HID from the Link or BYOH board. c027, c029
  • Hardware mode is what unlocks mouse-movement transforms, per-device binds, a nicknamed second keyboard as a macro pad, and Steady Hand movement filtering. c031, c033, c034, c035
  • Controllers work only in hardware mode, with a Rebind Link or BYOH whose USB profile includes a joypad. The default USB profile is keyboard and mouse only. c032, c005; docs: Hardware Setup Rebind knows the button layouts of wired and dongle Xbox controllers, DualShock 3, DualShock 4, DualSense, and Switch controllers, and of controllers that present as one of them; other controllers' buttons are named Joy1 to Joy32. They all work in hardware mode, with a Rebind Link or BYOH whose USB profile includes a joypad. docs: SDK Controllers (https://docs.rebind.gg/reference/sdk-reference#controllers)
  • Scripts still run on your computer. Link is not onboard keyboard firmware and doesn't run without the Rebind app. c022, c023
  • Rebind Link: a pre-flashed Teensy 4.0 in a snap-fit case, with a 0.5 m braided Micro-B cable. c042
  • BYOH (bring your own hardware): firmware and a license for a Teensy 4.0 or 4.1 you already own. The key arrives by email and you flash the board in the Rebind app. c046, c047

3. Demo-ready video ideas

Every idea is something Rebind documents today. Start each demo by showing the kill switch: Left Ctrl + Left Alt + K on Windows, Left Control + Left Option + K on macOS. It stops every script and releases held input, in both modes, on both systems. c063, c064, c065 Ideas marked Hardware need Rebind Link or BYOH; say so on screen.

Frame 05, "Kill switch." Caption on the frame: Simulated UI / animated mock-up.

Productivity

P1. One line of Luau: Caps Lock becomes Escape (software mode)

  • Hook: "This is the whole script. One line, and Caps Lock is Escape." c061
  • Show: install, then the quickstart in software mode with no account for local scripts and no hardware, then rb.bind.remap("CapsLock", "Escape"), Save, Run. Then add a chord remap. c024, c060, c061, c062
  • Note: installing Rebind is step one; the script doing the visible thing is the payoff. Windows installs from an Administrator PowerShell; macOS needs the Accessibility permission. c014, c058, c059

Frame 01, "Remap a key." Caption on the frame: Simulated UI / animated mock-up.

P2. Your mouse's side buttons, a different job in every app (software mode)

  • Hook: "Same two buttons. Undo and redo in my editor, something else in my browser." c067, c072
  • Show: one script targeted with process=, a second for another app, and the buttons switching jobs as you change windows. Optional: a key that brings your editor to the front when it's already running. c067, c068, c072, c073; SDK ref
  • Note: on macOS, window control is partial, so demo app switching on Windows or keep it to process= targeting. c019

Controller remaps (desktop demo, no game on screen)

G2. Your controller as a desktop remote (hardware mode)

  • Hook: "I wrote a few lines of Luau, and now my controller switches browser tabs." docs: Controllers
  • Show: an example script you write yourself, based on the docs recipe "Buttons as keyboard keys" (https://docs.rebind.gg/cookbook/controllers#buttons-as-keyboard-keys). In that recipe, rb.bind.remap("PadLB", "LCtrl+LShift+Tab") and rb.bind.remap("PadRB", "LCtrl+Tab") switch browser tabs, and A and B send Enter and Escape to confirm and cancel dialogs. These are bindings you write, not a built-in mapping. Film only desktop apps; no game on screen. Rehearse it on the current build. c030; docs: Controllers
  • Must say: this needs hardware mode, with a Rebind Link or BYOH whose USB profile includes a joypad. The default USB profile is keyboard and mouse only, so add a joypad first: https://docs.rebind.gg/getting-started/hardware-setup#change-the-usb-identity c032; docs: Hardware Setup If viewers later use controller scripts in games, they should follow each game's rules. c112

Thumbnail template 04, for G2. Placeholder template; add your own photo.

Accessibility

A1. Hold Shift without holding Shift (recipes; Steady Hand is Hardware)

  • Hook: "Five accessibility scripts for the keyboard and mouse you already own." c085, c116
  • Show: sticky modifiers, a one-handed layer, dwell-click, click assist, and debounce from the Accessibility recipes, each tuned in the script's settings. c085, c116 Optional hardware segment: Steady Hand movement filtering with Link or BYOH. c035
  • Must say: "These are scripts, not a medical treatment." c086, c035 Show what each recipe does; don't say who it will help or what it will fix.

Excel

E1. An Excel-only shortcut layer on keys you already have (software mode; macro-pad variant is Hardware)

  • Hook: "These buttons do Excel things in Excel, and nothing anywhere else." c072
  • Show: a script targeted to Excel with process=, mouse buttons or spare keys remapped to the Excel shortcuts you use most, a recorded keystroke macro, and text expansion for things you type often. c072, c062, c067, c069, c076 Hardware variant: a second keyboard or numpad nicknamed as a macro pad, so your main numpad still types digits. c034, c033
  • Must say: Rebind sends keystrokes; it doesn't control Excel's object model. Don't compare it to VBA or AutoHotkey COM automation.

Frame 04, "One key, whole shortcut." The shortcuts shown are examples. Caption on the frame: Simulated UI / animated mock-up.

Streaming

S1. The keys you already own, working like Stream Deck buttons (software mode)

  • Hook: "A Stream Deck adds keys. Rebind reprograms the ones you have." c105
  • Show: keys or mouse buttons switching OBS scenes through OBS hotkeys or through rb.net over the OBS WebSocket, and a spare key that brings OBS to the front when it's already running. c106, c074; SDK ref
  • Fair comparison (verifiable): Rebind uses keys you already own, adds remaps and per-app layers, and can be driven from official TypeScript, Python, and Rust clients. c105, c072, c080 A Stream Deck has dedicated labeled keys; Rebind doesn't replace those. Using both is fine.

Frame 03, "Bring your editor to the front from a spare key." The app must already be running; this does not start it. Caption on the frame: Simulated UI / animated mock-up.

S2. Show viewers what you're pressing (software mode)

  • Hook: "Keystrokes on screen, from a marketplace script." c092, c093
  • Show: installing Keystroke Overlay (@rebind/keystroke-overlay) or Input Display (@itzchill/input-display) from the Rebind marketplace, as a second step after installing the app. c091, c092, c093, c077
  • Note: on Windows, overlays don't draw over exclusive full-screen games, so capture in windowed or borderless mode. c020

5. Fair-use talking points and the claims fence

Talking points you can use

  • "Command, don't configure." c003
  • "Vendor software lets you select behavior. Rebind lets you write it." c008
  • "A Stream Deck adds keys. Rebind reprograms the ones you have." c105
  • "Rebind is free on Windows and macOS. No hardware required for key, button, and scroll remaps and macros." c012, c113
  • "Add Rebind Link, $140 once, if you need real USB HID, mouse-movement transforms, or a controller as a joypad." c041, c029, c031, c032 Price as of Nov 13, 2026; confirm on www.rebind.gg before publishing.
  • "Keep AutoHotkey. Move the jobs that need macOS, networking, or hardware output to Rebind. Your AHK files don't run as-is." c115, c095
  • "If you live on macOS, keep Karabiner and add Rebind for cross-OS and hardware-backed work." c098
  • "It works with the standard-HID keyboard and mouse you already own, any brand. It doesn't replace your keyboard's firmware or your RGB app." c116
  • "Rebind is designed for productivity, automation, accessibility, and legitimate input device applications." c109

Your channel, your call

  • Your opinion stays yours.
  • If Rebind sent you a unit or pays for content, disclose it clearly in the video itself (spoken and on screen) and use YouTube's paid-promotion label. A free unit counts.
  • Sponsorships and paid content are discussed case by case. This kit has no rates or terms.

Claims fence: say this, not that

Say Don't say
Supported today: Windows 10/11 64-bit and macOS 13+ on Apple Silicon. c013, c015 "Works on any PC," or any other platform or chip.
"Android and iOS apps are in development." c117 Any mobile date, feature, store link, price, or "coming soon."
Controllers work in hardware mode, with a Rebind Link or BYOH whose USB profile includes a joypad. c032; docs: Hardware Setup Controllers in software mode, or "works with every controller."
"Switch controllers" "Joy-Con"
Mouse movement, F13-F24, and media keys as input need Link or BYOH. c031, c036 Those features in the free app.
Accessibility recipes are scripts, not a medical treatment. c086 Treats, prevents, or fixes RSI, tremor, or any condition; replaces assistive tech or medical advice.
Use both: keep AutoHotkey, Karabiner, or your Stream Deck. c094, c098, c105 "Replaces AutoHotkey / Stream Deck / Karabiner," .ahk runs as-is, or Excel COM / VBA parity. c095
"Follow each game's rules. Rebind is not an anti-cheat bypass and does not promise you will not be penalized." c112 Undetectable, anti-cheat safe, bypass, ban-proof, rapid-fire, recoil, aim, turbo, or ranked or competitive advantage.
Mac window control is partial. c019 Full window control on macOS.
RebindGPT and AI need Pro. c096, c050 Free AI porting or free RebindGPT.
The app is free; installing a marketplace script is a separate step. c012, c091 That installing the app installs a script.
Rebind's own prices, as listed on rebind.gg (as of Nov 13, 2026; confirm on www.rebind.gg before publishing). c041, c046, c049 Competitor prices, user counts, time saved, percentages, or growth numbers.
— Affiliate rates, commission percentages, sponsorship amounts, or budgets.
— Partnerships with or endorsements from Elgato, Microsoft, Apple, or any other vendor.

Capture tips

  • Resolution: record at 1920×1080 or higher, at your usual frame rate. Zoom the editor to about 150% so code reads on a phone screen.
  • Clean desktop: close unrelated apps, hide desktop icons, and turn on Do Not Disturb so no notifications pop up.
  • Hide personal info: no email, messages, file paths with your name, browser tabs, bookmarks, account pages, license keys, or sign-in and activation screens.
  • Kill switch: if it helps the demo, show Left Ctrl + Left Alt + K (macOS: Left Control + Left Option + K) and say what it does: it stops every script and releases held input. c063, c064
  • Captions: add captions and check them by hand, especially Rebind, Luau, BYOH, and key names. Hold each result on screen for at least 3 seconds.
  • Platform in frame: only Windows 10/11 64-bit or macOS 13+ on Apple Silicon. c013, c015
  • Hardware shots: label them "Hardware mode · Rebind Link or BYOH." c031, c032

c001 Rebind is the programmable layer for computer input.
c002 Rebind is a programmable input layer, supported today on Windows and macOS, that lets you script your keyboard and mouse with Luau.
c003 Rebind's headline is "Command, don't configure."
c004 Rebind lets you rewrite keys and clicks in Luau.
c005 Adding Rebind Link lets you drive the mouse, and gamepads when the Link USB profile includes a joypad, as real USB HID.
↳ c005 note Use as: hardware mode, with a Rebind Link or BYOH whose USB profile includes a joypad.
c008 Vendor software lets you select behavior. Rebind lets you write it.
c012 The Rebind app is free.
c013 Rebind is supported today on Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit.
c014 Installing Rebind on Windows uses an Administrator PowerShell.
c015 Rebind is supported today on macOS 13 or later, on Apple Silicon only.
c017 The same Rebind scripts move between Windows and macOS, but not every API is identical on both.
c018 rb.pipe and rb.registry are Windows-only.
c019 rb.window is only partially supported on macOS.
c020 On Windows, rb.overlay does not draw over exclusive full-screen games.
c022 Rebind scripts run on the computer in both software mode and hardware mode.
c023 Rebind Link is not onboard keyboard firmware and does not run without the Rebind app.
c024 Software mode is free, needs no hardware, and needs no account for local scripts.
c025 Hardware mode uses Rebind Link or BYOH with a signed-in account and device activation.
c026 In software mode, Rebind captures input through operating-system hooks.
c027 In hardware mode, the attached keyboard, mouse and controllers are forwarded into an isolated capture VM before events reach scripts.
c028 In software mode, Rebind sends output through SendInput on Windows or CGEvent on macOS.
c029 In hardware mode, output is real USB HID from the Link or BYOH board.
c030 Both software mode and hardware mode can remap and block keys, buttons and scroll.
c031 Mouse-movement transforms, such as a move handler or mouse_block=true, need hardware mode; in software mode Rebind refuses to start the script.
c032 Game controller and joypad output needs hardware mode and a Link USB profile that includes a joypad.
↳ c032 note Use as: hardware mode, with a Rebind Link or BYOH whose USB profile includes a joypad.
c033 Telling devices apart and per-device binds need hardware mode; in software mode the device is nil.
c034 A device-split pad, such as a nicknamed second keyboard, needs hardware mode.
c035 Steady Hand movement and tremor filtering needs hardware mode and is a supported recipe, not a medical treatment.
c036 Pressing F13-F24, Menu, media and volume keys as input reaches Rebind only with a Link or BYOH; on macOS, MediaStop and F21-F24 are not available.
c038 The free Rebind app sees input through OS hooks before your apps do.
c041 Rebind Link costs $140, one payment.
c042 Rebind Link is a pre-flashed Teensy 4.0 in a snap-fit case with a 0.5 m braided Micro-B cable.
c043 Rebind Link ships free to the US and Canada only.
c046 Rebind BYOH costs $90, one time, for firmware and a license for a Teensy 4.0 or 4.1 the buyer already owns.
c047 The BYOH license key arrives by email, and the buyer flashes the board in the Rebind app.
c048 Outside the US and Canada, BYOH is the hardware option, because Rebind Link ships to the US and Canada only.
c049 Rebind Pro costs $9 per month or $72 per year.
c050 Rebind Pro includes AI, rb.ai, rb.phone and creating cloud backups.
c051 Rebind Pro is not required for hardware mode, remaps or macros.
c053 Rebind Pro has one 7-day trial per email.
c054 Activating a Rebind Link or BYOH license adds 12 months of Pro, which ends unless you buy Pro.
c058 On Windows, you install Rebind by running irm https://rebind.gg/install.ps1
c059 On macOS, you install Rebind by running curl -fsSL https://rebind.gg/install.sh
c060 The Rebind quickstart runs in software mode with no account and no hardware.
↳ c060 note Use as: no account for local scripts.
c061 The first documented Rebind script is rb.bind.remap("CapsLock", "Escape").
c062 rb.bind.remap can map a key to a chord, such as Kp1 to LCtrl+LAlt+1.
c063 Rebind's kill switch is Left Ctrl + Left Alt + K on Windows and Left Control + Left Option + K on macOS.
c064 The kill switch stops every script and releases held input.
c065 The kill switch works in both modes on both Windows and macOS.
c067 Software mode supports key remaps with rb.bind.remap and key, button and scroll handlers with rb.on.
c068 In software mode, Rebind handles mouse buttons, not mouse movement.
c069 You can record macros in the Rebind app and play them with rb.macro.
c070 Rebind scripts can use Luau coroutines: rb.run, rb.sleep and rb.async.
c072 Rebind scripts can target specific apps with a process= or window= modeline or a when callback.
c073 A targeted Rebind script can use focus and blur handlers to behave differently per app.
c074 Rebind has built-in networking with rb.net.get, rb.net.post, rb.net.listen and rb.net.ws_listen.
c076 Text expansion is available in Rebind as a productivity cookbook recipe.
c077 Rebind scripts can draw overlays with rb.overlay.
c078 Rebind has UI panels with rb.ui, plus overlay, screen, window and macro APIs.
c079 Rebind supports local WebSocket remote control.
c080 Rebind has official TypeScript, Python and Rust clients.
c081 Rebind has an MCP server for agent input.
c082 Rebind scripts can be shipped as encrypted bytecode sealed to one device or one buyer.
c083 Rebind marketplace purchases can be one-time or subscription.
c084 Rebind has private, invite-only Channels.
c085 Rebind accessibility recipes include dwell-click, click assist, debounce, sticky modifiers and one-handed layers.
c086 Rebind's accessibility recipes are scripts, not a medical treatment.
c087 Rebind scripts are plain .lua or .luau files in %APPDATA%\Rebind\scripts on Windows and ~/Library/Application Support/Rebind/scripts on macOS.
c088 You can edit Rebind scripts in an external editor such as VS Code, organize them in subfolders, and track them with git.
c090 A third-party Rebind script runs only within the permissions the user approved.

c093 Input Display is the @itzchill/input-display script on the Rebind marketplace.
c094 Use both: keep your AutoHotkey library and move what should run on hardware to Rebind.

c098 If you live on macOS, keep Karabiner and add Rebind for cross-OS and hardware-backed work.
c102 Rebind remaps any standard-HID USB keyboard or mouse.
c103 Rebind is brand-neutral for standard-HID keyboards and mice.
c104 Use the vendor app for RGB and onboard profiles; Rebind leaves lighting alone.
c105 A Stream Deck adds keys. Rebind reprograms the ones you have.
